headline: OSPF configuration added and interface Gi2 shutdown
executive_summary: A configuration change was applied to R1 that enables OSPF routing for the 192.168.1.1 network while simultaneously shutting down the interface (GigabitEthernet2) associated with that network. This creates a contradiction where the routing protocol is configured for a disabled interface, which will prevent the OSPF adjacency from forming.
technical_summary: Added 'router ospf 1' with network 192.168.1.1/32 in area 0. Interface GigabitEthernet2 was updated with a description and set to 'shutdown'.
risk_reason: The configuration change shuts down the interface that the newly configured OSPF process is attempting to use, which will result in a routing failure for the internal peer.
potential_impact: Loss of connectivity to the internal routing peer on GigabitEthernet2. OSPF adjacency will fail to establish.
validation_checks: show ip interface brief | include GigabitEthernet2
recommended_action: Verify if the shutdown of GigabitEthernet2 was intentional. If connectivity to the internal peer is required, remove the 'shutdown' command from the interface.
rollback_recommendation: Remove the 'router ospf 1' configuration and remove the 'shutdown' command from GigabitEthernet2 if the interface was intended to be active.
anomalies: OSPF configured on a shutdown interface
